elements.element: Customer owns deliverables created for it.
elements.evidence: Section 5.5 states that, as between the Parties, the Company owns all deliverables created by or for HDI for the Company under the Agreement.

elements.element: Customer owns work product created for it.
elements.evidence: Section 5.5 expressly gives the Company all right, title and interest in work product created by or for HDI for the Company under the Agreement.

elements.element: Vendor assigns its rights in the deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: HDI expressly assigns to the Company all right, title and interest it may have in the deliverables and work product.

elements.element: Vendor retains ownership of its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that HDI retains all right, title and interest in its pre-existing intellectual property.

elements.element: Customer receives a licence to Vendor intellectual property embedded in the deliverables.
elements.evidence: HDI grants the Company a licence to any HDI intellectual property embedded in the deliverables.

elements.element: The embedded Vendor IP licence is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The embedded-IP licence is expressly described as perpetual.

elements.element: The embedded Vendor IP licence is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The embedded-IP licence is expressly described as irrevocable.

elements.element: The embedded Vendor IP licence is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The embedded-IP licence is expressly described as royalty-free.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The clause protects only user, customer, order and transaction data collected through or generated by the Site. It does not cover all data supplied, owned or controlled by the Company, including Company data outside that Site-specific definition.

elements.element: No joint ownership of intellectual property is created.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that nothing in the Agreement creates joint ownership of intellectual property.

elements.element: Vendor owns generic tools.
elements.evidence: HDI retains only pre-existing intellectual property. The clause does not reserve ownership of generic tools generally and may assign generic tools developed as deliverables or work product to the Company.

elements.element: Vendor owns know-how.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no ownership reservation for HDI know-how, including know-how developed during performance.

elements.element: Customer receives a licence to the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The Company receives the stronger right of ownership in the deliverables, together with a licence to embedded HDI intellectual property.

elements.element: The licence to the deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The Company's ownership is not time-limited, and the licence covering embedded HDI intellectual property is expressly perpetual.

elements.element: The licence to the deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The assignment is not stated to be revocable, and the licence covering embedded HDI intellectual property is expressly irrevocable.

elements.element: The licence to the deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: Neither the assignment nor the embedded-IP licence expressly states that the rights are worldwide.

elements.element: The licence to the deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The deliverables are assigned without any reserved royalty, and the licence covering embedded HDI intellectual property is expressly royalty-free.

elements.element: Customer may use the deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Ownership of the deliverables and the unrestricted embedded-IP licence permit the Company to use the deliverables for its business.

elements.element: Customer may modify the deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Although ownership supports modification of the assigned material, the licence to embedded HDI intellectual property does not expressly include modification rights, so the right to modify the complete deliverables is not assured.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense the deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: The licence to embedded HDI intellectual property does not expressly permit sublicensing, so the Company cannot be assured of sublicensing the complete deliverables.

result.reason: The redline substantially implements the preferred ownership structure, but its data definition is limited to specified Site-collected or Site-generated data and therefore does not protect all Customer Data. It also fails the fallback because it does not reserve generic tools and know-how to HDI and omits express worldwide, modification and sublicensing rights for embedded HDI IP. The unrelated General Manager language remains intact, but neither position is completely achieved.
